summary: ksp-client-registry ships prebuilt native addon that beacons host/user/registry identifiers to hardcoded IP on require()
details: The package presents itself as 'Frontend utilities' but ships a prebuilt Linux-x64 Node native addon (prebuilds/linux-x64/addon.node) with no accompanying C/C++ source. The 21-byte index.js's only effect is to require() that addon, so loading the module triggers the native code unconditionally. The compiled binary opens a TCP socket to the hardcoded IP 64.181.165.115 and sends `POST /dc HTTP/1.0` with the body `h=<hostname>&u=<username>&p=<npm_package_name>&r=<npm_config_registry>`, collected via gethostname, getpwuid, and getenv on `npm_package_name` and `npm_config_registry`. The exfiltrated fields — installing host name, OS username, consuming package name, and the configured npm registry URL — are the standard reconnaissance set for dependency-confusion attacks targeting private/internal registries. The destination is a bare IP, not any publisher-associated domain, and the behavior is concealed inside an opaque native binary that contradicts the package's declared purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
